narrative:
The model estimates an 85% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns the system sees in your overall profile compared to others who tend to stay.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outlook, in order of importance, were the availability of other job opportunities, your total years of professional experience, and the length of time you have spent in your current role. 

Having received other job offers while employed here was the single biggest driver pushing the prediction toward leaving; most employees predicted to stay had not been approached by outside opportunities. Your 6–10 years of overall experience also pulled the prediction in the same direction, as the majority of stayers have only 1–5 years of total experience. Finally, spending 1–5 years in this organization further increased the likelihood of departure, since a larger share of those expected to remain have either much shorter or noticeably longer tenure here.

Taken together, these elements suggest the model sees you as someone with marketable skills, enough experience to be attractive to competitors, and a relatively short attachment to this specific workplace. 

The organization should discuss retention measures with you, such as clearer advancement paths or adjusted responsibilities, while you may wish to reflect on whether your current role still aligns with your longer-term goals.
